analysis.title: Schroders Credit Lens USD, November 2026
key_insights: Credit spreads widened in October 2026, especially in Europe. USD IG OAS is 94bps (16th percentile of 20 years), EUR IG 104bps (31st), GBP IG 98bps (11th), USD HY 344bps (21st), EUR HY 359bps (34th), Hard EMD 208bps (5th), Corp EMD 204bps (10th).
Spreads exceed long-term default and downgrade losses. Risk premium after those losses is 0.6% for USD IG, 0.7% for EUR IG, 1.6% for USD HY, 2.0% for EUR HY, 0.8% for Hard EMD and 1.1% for Corp EMD.

Margin of safety (how far spreads can rise over 12 months before the credit spread is wiped out) is 15bps for USD IG vs a 20-year average of 23, 23bps for EUR IG vs 30, 90bps for USD HY vs 108, and 102bps for EUR HY vs 128. Schroders says higher spreads have normalised it in HY and EUR IG.

Higher yields let bonds absorb a bigger yield rise over 12 months before absolute returns turn negative. Yields to worst: cash 4.0%, Treasuries 4.8%, IG corporates 5.8%, Corp EMD 6.9%, Hard EMD 7.1%, HY 8.3%.

Big tech/hyperscaler bond borrowing continues to rise rapidly. Hyperscaler IG spreads are rising versus the broader US IG market, and tech (including hyperscalers) is a growing share of the US IG index.
Hyperscaler issuance raises index duration because they issue long-dated bonds. Durations cited: Alphabet 8.8, Amazon 8.0, Meta 9.2, Oracle 7.5, against 5.8 for the US IG index.

Other USD IG issuers responded to higher rates by issuing shorter-dated bonds. The 1-5yr share of gross issuance ex-hyperscalers is 43%, 5-10yr is 36% and 10+yr is 22%. The net result is that USD IG maturity and duration are low versus history.

Schroders' 100-year analysis finds Baa spreads over Treasuries were at similar or tighter levels than today for much of the 1940s-60s. High government debt lowers the Treasury 'convenience yield' premium, which narrows spreads, and that condition applies now.

Of five historical drivers of tight spreads, only high government debt clearly applies today. Near-zero defaults are unlikely, and institutional demand cannot expand on the same scale. Utilities are now a small share of a more cyclical market, so spreads should be higher than in the past.
Policy-driven demand for credit (financial repression, Regulation Q) could recur in a different form. Schroders says yield curve control may not be necessary but is not off the table.

Conclusion for investors: hold-to-maturity strategic buyers have less reason to wait. Tactical investors have a thin margin of safety, since a small spread rise would make corporates underperform governments. Active selection is favored because spreads barely distinguish good borrowers from bad.
FX-hedged yields: USD IG 5.8%, EUR IG 5.8%, GBP IG corporates 6.2%, EUR HY 8.4%, USD HY 8.3%. Euro investors in USD IG get 4.2% and Japanese investors 2.8%.
Fundamentals: leverage is on a rising trend even though profitability and earnings growth are strong. Default rates are low and HY distress ratios show relative calm.
Spread dispersion within HY has increased. US HY net downgrades have outpaced upgrades for the last three months running, while fallen angels and rising stars have offset each other.

IG issuance is very high in 2026. The sterling IG market is shrinking while USD and EUR expand. The EUR HY market had contracted but high 2025-26 issuance has reversed that. The HY ratings mix keeps improving.
Total returns to 31 Oct 2026: USD IG +2.0% in one month, -0.8% YTD, -0.5% over one year. USD HY +0.3% in one month, +0.3% YTD, +1.5% over one year. EUR HY -1.0% in one month (USD hedged -0.9%).

sector_views.rationale: Tech is a growing share of the index and hyperscaler spreads are widening versus the market. Schroders says building fundamental fragility can take a while to play out.
Utilities are a small share of today's more cyclical bond market, so spreads should be higher than in past eras of low spreads.

macro_indicators.indicator: US HY par default rate (trailing 12 months)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Defaults are low, which supports spreads. Near-zero defaults like the post-war era are unlikely.
High debt lowers the Treasury convenience yield, raises Treasury yields relative to corporates and narrows credit spreads.

risk_factors: Tight spreads leave little margin of safety. A small spread rise would push corporates below government bonds, especially for tactical investors who buy now and sell later.
Collateral damage to some sectors from an AI boom could raise credit risk.
Politics is becoming entangled with monetary policy, with possible Treasury market effects that spill into corporate bonds.
Hyperscaler debt is growing as a share of the index and its spreads are rising versus the market.
vol_and_positioning: Spread dispersion in US HY and Euro HY has increased.
HY distress ratios (share of issues above 1,000bp) show relative calm.
US HY net downgrades have outpaced upgrades for three months running.

tension_points.bull_case: Spreads comfortably exceed long-term default and downgrade losses, with risk premia of 0.6% for USD IG and 1.6% for USD HY. Historical precedent exists for spreads to stay tight for decades, and high government debt is an under-appreciated supporting factor.
tension_points.bear_case: Tight spreads leave little margin of safety. USD IG can absorb only 15bps of widening over 12 months before underperforming governments, against a 20-year average of 23bps.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A small rise in spreads would make corporate bonds underperform government bonds for tactical investors who buy now and sell later.

theme_stances.key_argument: Historical precedent exists for credit spreads to stay tighter than today for several decades, and high government debt is an under-appreciated driver.
theme_stances.evidence: Historical precedent exists for credit spreads to stay tighter than today

theme_stances.key_argument: Hyperscaler borrowing and spreads are rising and their index weight is growing, though fundamental fragility can take time to play out.
